text: The last mile was always the hardest, a rule Cassius had proven true on every long walk he'd ever undertaken and this one was no exception. His pack, {0} at the start of the day, had somehow grown heavier with every step despite containing exactly what it had that morning. A lamp came into view first, {2} against the dark, marking the edge of town before any of the buildings themselves did, and he fixed his eyes on it the way a sailor might fix on a lighthouse. He forced himself to keep his pace {3} rather than break into the run his body was suddenly, unreasonably, suggesting, saving what little dignity remained after a day like this one. When he finally reached the inn, he lowered himself into the nearest chair with a groan of pure {4} and did not attempt to move again for a considerable while.
